conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index and quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a reasonable growth outlook.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, increasing each to 6% to lean into leveraged ETFs.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It uses leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, which significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can lose a lot fast if stops are not strictly adhered to.

income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It prioritizes income and low drawdown by rotating into income ETFs and reducing high-beta names. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
